profile: static opaque palette-only; double-sided open thin leaf strips; no textures
scientific_status: evidence-informed stylized conifer architectural concept; no identified extinct species reconstruction
provenance: Original geometry. r12 wood coordinates and faces retained exactly, r17 A constructor retained unchanged. References consulted only; no external mesh or imagery incorporated.
artistic_choices: The user explicitly selected separated, feathery, airy A rather than B connected feather-core surfaces. Natural sparsity and sky windows are intended style, not a density defect by itself.
Paired local lower-crown attachments and inherited r18 upper arrangement produce irregular layered foliage. The existing broken lower bough remains.
Individual-like needle count, enlarged groups, colors, seven-meter scale and precise branch arrangement are artistic abstractions, not measured fossil anatomy.
topology_notes: Main wood remains closed flat-shaded geometry with original collars. Upper fine supports are8 triangles per spray. Leaves are intentionally open double-sided opaque strips, with two gently bent panels and shared normals. No thick green tube, ridge-filled hard blade or connected B core. Organic twig/branch contacts are intentionally buried intersections.
source_vertex_count_convention: Sum of authored unique mesh vertices, no modifiers or instances.
target_runtime: Three.js0.180.0; exact GPU and composed-scene evidence pending separate gate.

description.en: An airy seven-meter conifer concept with rounded tapering main boughs, separated narrow feather-like needle sprays, shallow local overlap and natural crown sky windows.
